messages:
Maya (Billing): FYI got an escalated ticket from Support — ACME mid-cycle downgrade but they insist on a PO for any payout. Card refund blocked by customer policy. Can we do a partial credit note + FX adjustment?
Javier (Support): Customer switched from Team Pro (EUR 10k/mo) -> Team Standard (EUR 7k/mo) on 2026-03-09, billing cycle 1st-31st. They expect the prorated difference on next invoice. Their AP requires a credit note (no direct refunds).
Ellie (Accounting): Ok. The tricky part: original charge was billed in EUR, their accounting wants USD amounts on the credit note and our ledger shows USD because of accounting region. Exchange rate movement created a small delta.
Samir (Finance): Do we have a policy for issuing credit notes when currency conversion creates fractional cents? We want the credited USD to exactly offset the receivable. If we issue the EUR amount on a credit note, the customer's AP can still process it, but our books need the USD FX journal.
Maya (Billing): Current options:
1) Issue EUR credit note for the prorated EUR amount (preferred for customer PO) and post an internal FX gain/loss journal to reconcile to our USD ledger.
2) Issue USD credit note (requires PO wording change and legal sign-off) — slower.
3) Manual refund to card (not allowed per customer PO).
Javier (Support): Customer confirmed they will only accept a credit note with PO #PO-4491 visible on the document. Can we add PO field to the credit note PDF?
Maya (Billing): billing-bot can attach PO number. billing-bot: Generated draft credit note CN-2026-045 (EUR) for invoice INV-2026-1123, amount EUR 3,000. Draft available at /internal/billing/drafts/CN-2026-045.
Ellie (Accounting): I ran the quick calc. Their prorated EUR difference = 3000 EUR but using our book rate at settlement gives USD 3,243.27, while the refund-side conversion at time of refund would have been USD 3,238.59 -> delta USD 4.68.
Ellie (Accounting): Code snippet I used:
```
prorated_eur = (10000 - 7000) * days_left / days_in_cycle  # = 3000 * 22/31 = 2129.03? (example)
# For full-month example we used 3000 EUR
usd_book = round(3000 * 1.08109, 2)  # = 3243.27
usd_refund = round(3000 * 1.07953, 2)  # = 3238.59
fx_delta = usd_book - usd_refund  # = 4.68
```
Maya (Billing): Proposed flow: issue EUR credit note with PO attached, post CN to customer account, then create a one-line FX adjustment journal to clear the USD mismatch. That preserves customer AP workflow and keeps our GL tidy.
Samir (Finance): Sounds fine. Need approval from Finance to post the FX journal. Amount is small < $5 but need docs. Ellie, please prepare JE: debit FX loss 4.68, credit AR 4.68 with reference CN-2026-045.
Ellie (Accounting): Will do. Also recommend adding a note on the credit note PDF: "Credit issued for mid-cycle plan downgrade; USD conversion at book rate applied. See internal JE 2026-FX-078." Customer PO can remain visible.
Javier (Support): I told the customer: we'll issue the credit note (with PO) by EOD and apply the small FX reconciliation internally. They're happy with that.
Maya (Billing): Action items:
- billing-bot: publish CN-2026-045 (EUR) with PO-4491 on PDF (Maya)
- Ellie: create JE 2026-FX-078 and route to Samir for sign-off
- Support: confirm to customer when CN published (Javier)
billing-bot: Published CN-2026-045 PDF to /internal/billing/issued/CN-2026-045.pdf with PO field set to PO-4491.
Samir (Finance): Approved JE 2026-FX-078, sign-off recorded.
Maya (Billing): Closing loop — credit applied to customer account today, will reduce next invoice. Marking thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
